sourceBaseline.interpretation: The TypeScript wallet-auth page is compatibility context only; A1.9 does not execute it or claim complete connector, network-switching, browser, accessibility, or production parity.

implementationBase.interpretation: Immutable branch snapshot immediately before the A1.9 frontend auth-recovery UX implementation.

invariants.claim: The exact A1.8 contract, verifier and twelve-file evidence inventory replay successfully from commit c238954c without applying A1.9 files to the historical proof.
Only the frontend auth route receives a closed signed-out, recovering or verifier-unavailable state, and recovery requires missing-or-rejected access plus the frontend BFF's own refresh cookie.
The recovering auth page is aria-busy, exposes a live status with fixed restoration copy, and disables wallet connection until recovery resolves.
Verifier unavailability renders a fixed nondisclosing alert, disables wallet sign-in and never emits the automatic recovery bootstrap.
A genuinely signed-out auth page keeps the wallet action enabled and exposes neither recovery progress nor a verifier-outage claim.
Unknown server states render verifier-unavailable, and a recovery-failure event is accepted only while the page is exactly recovering.
The fixed recovery bootstrap emits exactly the closed version-one failed event after rejection and interpolates no credential, identity, wallet, error or policy value.
A valid recovery failure hides progress, focuses a fixed alert, clears aria-busy and enables a Try Again wallet action without reflecting event payload.
A wallet click immediately shows Opening wallet, hides stale errors, disables duplicate activation and marks the page busy without performing independent wallet or network work.
A1.8 page-lifetime single-flight, shared session-mutation lock, rotation-attested reload, confirmed-clear navigation, no-retry and token-free browser rules remain structurally intact.
Recovery-bearing HTML stays private no-store and credential-varying, the offline shell stays public and recovery-free, and unsupported operational or customer-count claims remain absent.
A1.9 adds no permission, plan, ranking-offset, feature-flag, subscription or entitlement authority and authorizes no live or production action.

hermeticTests.exactName: rejected recovery emits one exact closed event
resolved recovery emits no failure event
invalid recovery events leave the recovering page closed
valid failure becomes fixed actionable UI without reflecting payload

residualStops.claim: No accepted real-browser matrix proves Web Locks, BroadcastChannel, HttpOnly cookie application, reload, redirect, focus, event ordering or multi-tab scheduling.
No proxy or browser fault injection proves timeout or reset behavior after backend commit.
No PostgreSQL exercise proves consume, replay response, commit acknowledgement ambiguity or family-lock ordering.
A disconnect after backend rotation but before Set-Cookie delivery still forces reauthentication and has no receipt or idempotency protocol.
JavaScript cannot prove clearing HttpOnly cookies while the BFF itself is unreachable.
Already-issued access tokens remain valid until expiry after logout or family revocation.
A missing access cookie has no key ID to verify before recovery, so a later JWKS outage can still force reauthentication after rotation.
No real-browser proof or server-owned attempt guard excludes repeated reloads when refresh cookies are accepted while access cookies are selectively rejected or evicted.
No screen-reader, keyboard-only, reduced-motion or focus-order matrix validates the new status and alert transitions.
Injected-wallet behavior does not prove connector choice, wallet installation, chain switching, mobile wallets or provider-specific recovery.
No accepted screenshot or device matrix proves the signed-out, recovering, outage and recovery-failed layouts.
A1.9 changes only the frontend auth page and does not prove equivalent admin recovery UX.
Passing A1.9 integrity never authorizes a live browser, database, network, secret, service, deployment or production action.
